topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
As she walked to the new employee's workstation, Emma couldn't help but bounce with each step. Her bright yellow sundress seemed to glow in the fluorescent lights of the office, and her ponytail swung behind her like a metronome. She had never been one for grand gestures, but today felt different - like any moment now could be the catalyst for something amazing.

When she arrived at the cubicle, Emma found Rachel sitting with an open laptop, surrounded by scattered notes and pens. Emma plopped down beside her, almost as if they were old friends sharing a secret joke. "Okay, I've got your manuals right here," Emma said, rummaging through her bag for a binder full of handouts. "Let's get you up to warp speed on this stuff!"

As Rachel flipped through the pages, her brow furrowed in concentration. But Emma just nudged her, beaming with enthusiasm, and whispered, "I'll show you everything I know - all the hidden shortcuts and shortcuts within shortcuts." Rachel couldn't help but giggle at Emma's infectious grin.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Lena strolled into the conference room, coffee cup held high as if in a toast. It was her last day on the team, and she'd convinced everyone to let her take the reins for training their newbie, Leo. The sunlight streaming through the French windows highlighted the soft curls framing her face as she winked at him. "Alright, kiddo, time to break me," Lena declared.

Leo looked stunned, but Lena just clapped him on the back and guided him into the fold of her sweater, like they were about to share a top-secret plan. As she outlined Leo's tasks, he scribbled furiously while his eyes darted toward Lena with admiration. When he hesitated over a tricky problem, Lena pounced – whispering reassurances that only seemed to fuel his focus.

By the time they'd exhausted their list of duties, Lena had produced a makeshift schedule for Leo and assigned himself two weeks' leave, claiming it was all part of "transitioning out smoothly". The real reason, however? She couldn't bear to tear herself away from this impromptu reunion.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Alexa's fingers flew over the keyboard, typing out an entire PowerPoint presentation in one go. At least, that's what she thought - it was probably just wishful thinking now that her job would soon be taken over by Jack, a smooth-talking young thing fresh off some ivy league college. Yet something about his eager gaze still managed to disarm Alexa.

When the team decided to stage a mock handover, Alexa insisted on leading from the front. With every step she took toward Jack's desk, the air in her lungs seemed to grow lighter - almost as if it actually did float away when people found themselves at ease with each other. She introduced herself like anyone else, but instead of hiding behind the formal title they'd all shared, Alexa leaned against the table and began pointing out 'shortcuts nobody knew about' – a phrase that earned Jack an impressed raise of his brow.

Over lunch, they dived head-first into strategies, mapping them out together. The room shook ever so slightly beneath their feet, probably due to another office rumble, but for all intents and purposes, the world felt slightly more wobbled while leaning on its axis – not that anyone noticed or anything.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Morgan stood up straight as she watched Emily unpacking a new laptop into her station. He remembered days back when that was his desk and how anxious he'd felt taking it over from an outgoing colleague (he still had the stress ball in question buried deep within a dusty storage bin behind reception). For reasons unknown, he found himself grinning today.

By 11 am, their impromptu office café meeting transformed into the world's smallest onboarding session. Morgan poured coffee cups for Emily like they were sharing an inside joke rather than discussing some corporate protocol he was well-acquainted with - one of many intricacies that normally caused her colleagues' eyes to glaze over during meetings.

"I wish I'd done this when you first joined," Emily said, beaming at him from over her own new steamer cup. "I'd have saved myself so much heartache." Morgan felt the words tickle the corner of his mouth where he liked to store a lingering smile.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Rachel puffed out a happy sigh, feeling weight lift off those weary shoulders as she accepted Ben's challenge: become the company legend in mere weeks. At last, it would give them both an excuse to take a well-deserved holiday – even without that official job title anymore! Now all he needed was her secret to making colleagues feel included.

This time around Rachel had Ben sit down with her over sandwiches outside by the river while the clouds drifted lazily across its banks. They dangled tiny pieces of pizza dough above it, watching them twirl on air currents like wisps of leaves drifting without a destination: carefree as anything he'd ever experienced in this cramped city office building.

Each time Rachel shared an anecdote about Ben or another team member that brought their hands together at the wrist (or sometimes merely across fingers), Ben responded with wide-eyed surprise. That same curiosity began forming into something new – and when they strolled back to their desks later, Ben turned his face toward hers for what would be a long series of days until she left...

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Emily fidgeted with her pens, clicking the caps on and off as she stared at her manager's email. "Training Session Schedule" was emblazoned across the top of the page. Her heart rate increased slightly as she scanned through the list of employees who needed training. Her name was at the bottom. When was it that she would be handing over her responsibilities? The familiar ache in her shoulders reappeared, a tension she'd grown accustomed to since... well, ever. She rubbed them absently as she pondered what lay ahead.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Mark leaned back in his chair and let out a sigh as he stared at the new employee photo staring back at him from the company database. The young woman's bright smile seemed to leap off the screen, infesting every corner of his office with an unfamiliar sense of excitement. He squirmed, rearranging the stack of folders on his desk in what felt like the hundredth time that day. It was supposed to be a straightforward transition, but Mark couldn't shake the nagging sensation that he was about to get himself into trouble.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Rachel let out a low whistle as she scrolled through her email inbox for what felt like an eternity. Amidst all the standard office drivel lurked one crucial message: from HR to her boss. Something had triggered it—she knew she'd been around long enough to recognize the trigger, and it wasn't anything good for someone in her shoes. She bit back a laugh when she noticed her hands were clenched into awkward fist, which felt ridiculous since... everyone would just be doing it soon enough.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Lena tapped her toes against the worn wooden floor of her office as she wondered when they'd actually get to meet. The news had swept through her desk like wildfire – next to make room for fresh meat or blood... either way, she couldn't see herself being around much longer. As long as it was fair game, at least, and she could pass on what made the position worthwhile, then fine. It meant taking responsibility seriously enough that someone else wouldn't burn out within days of taking over.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Gabriel's eyes had a peculiar glaze as he walked down to his department meeting room. They'd never bothered with 'official' meetings before – the office hummed along just fine on whispers, but this one felt special. Not the kind of special that brought a bottle of wine in or anything that might lead to an actual solution; no, more like... this was his cue to wrap up his role neatly and give new hands something meaningful to grasp onto.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
As she led her trainee through the familiar corridors, Emma couldn't help but feel a sense of... unease. Her feet seemed rooted to the spot as she stood in front of the employee's workstation, watching her new colleague fumble with the computer mouse. She had always prided herself on being thorough and organized, so seeing someone struggle to replicate her systems was like watching a part of herself unravel.

The trainee looked up at her, confusion etched on her face, and Emma took a deep breath and attempted to mimic a calm demeanor. "Okay, let's start from the beginning," she began, trying not to sound too critical as she gestured for the trainee to follow her. As they walked through the office, Emma kept glancing over her shoulder, half-expectantly waiting for someone – or something – to confirm that this change was somehow a mistake.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
I adjusted my grip on the coffee cup in my hand and studied it intently, wondering why I wasn't trembling. My trainee stood across from me, nodding enthusiastically as I dictated the first steps of our project setup. Their eyes seemed genuinely interested, yet every word out of their mouth sounded like a practiced script.

When they made a mistake – and we're all human sometimes – I caught myself tensing up before forcing my shoulders to relax. This was what I'd been trained for; it wasn't about attachment or ownership of those numbers, outcomes, or deadlines; we were supposed to share this weight, after all. My job was just one chapter in their book. A part of me wanted to rewrite that script and rewrite it with the same level of finesse and dedication that I put into everything else.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Lena's hand shook ever so slightly as she handed over the phone to John. His eyes narrowed, as he took off his specs for a closer look before passing them back. Lena bit her lip hard enough for it to hurt and let out an awkward laugh while taking down some details. They worked on that new department together – him on weekends and her every other. Their boss had told Lena the time had come.

As John spoke about plans, his body language suggested patience; he didn't seem nervous or uncertain at all as he explained which tasks he'd be in charge of doing first. When she mentioned their own doubts she'd been having about sharing this kind of responsibility to a relative newbie, her words came out stilted. And what surprised Lena, was that John listened attentively without dismissing her fears.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Kareem's eyes snapped back into focus as the trainee raised an eyebrow at his instructions. The corner of Kareem's mouth twisted downward in self-mockery as the memories returned: he'd been put in this very same situation more than a year ago, and all these people thought they were experts now, after years... It was time to remember that there was supposed to be a learning curve.

"Uh-oh," the trainee muttered, frowning at her hand typing away. The keys clicked faster as the panic heightened in her voice. Kareem took control of the conversation and, through his tone, somehow he brought it back on track – an illusionary sense of peace spreading over the tension; they kept working like this until everything became just another task.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
As she closed her computer, Maria let out a quiet sigh and shifted her chair in her seat. Her gaze met that of her soon-to-be replacement across from her desk, their eyes matching – or so it felt, considering the unease knotting up inside Maria now more than ever before. She had worked alongside her trainee for weeks; yet as she thought about letting go of this particular responsibility...

The air thinned out a bit between them; but in place of discomfort was something hard to put into words... They stood there – two colleagues looking toward a near-invisible horizon and trying, somehow trying to understand how everything else would look from just her side of the desk.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
As she stood in front of her replacement, Emily's hands trembled slightly as she handed over the manuals. "Okay, so... um... let me walk you through this first." She took a deep breath and tried to compose herself.

Her heart felt like it was racing, and her mind kept wandering back to all the things that could go wrong. What if this new person couldn't handle the workload? What if she made mistakes because of it?

She forced a bright smile onto her face as she spoke, trying to reassure herself as much as her replacement. "Don't worry, I'll be here for you every step of the way."

The new employee nodded eagerly, eyes wide with enthusiasm. Emily tried to match their energy but couldn't shake off the feeling of unease growing inside her.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
She paced back and forth in front of her desk, fidgeting with a pen as she muttered to herself. "Why do I have to be the one to train someone new? Can't they just figure it out on their own?"

Laura's eyes darted towards the employee who would soon be taking over her responsibilities, but she quickly looked away, not wanting to make eye contact. She took a few more steps back and forth before remembering the stack of paperwork she needed to review.

The sound of her own breathing seemed amplified in the silence. The air conditioning unit above her desk whirred on, creating an eerie background hum that only added to her growing anxiety.

Laura forced herself to sit down and begin going through the reports, trying to focus on the task at hand instead of the looming possibility of losing her position.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
She leaned against the whiteboard, arms crossed over her chest as she watched the new employee scribble notes all over it. "Okay, so that's how you schedule the daily meetings," she said finally, voice tight with unease.

Margaret couldn't help but think of all the things she was going to miss out on – her lunch break, her morning coffee routine, even just sitting in this office and pretending everything was fine for a minute. It was strange; being gone from the job still felt like some kind of dream, not something that would actually happen.

The employee asked another question, but Margaret found herself struggling to remember what they had discussed previously. The room seemed to be tilting slightly to one side as she tried to focus on their conversation.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
As he stood in front of the new recruit, Jack's hands fumbled with the remote control of the conference room phone system all over again. "Yeah... just click this one button and it'll, uh, pick up."

The sound of his own voice seemed muffled to him, as if someone was speaking through a layer of cotton balls. He squinted slightly as he gestured towards the controls on the far wall.

"Right after that, there are five other devices... um... no, wait – just click one device then press save."

Jack's eyes scanned back and forth across his notes but kept landing on one specific word: ' terminated'. His gut lurched again at his own hand-writing squiggling over it so dramatically. He shook off the sensation as a mistake in itself.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Dr. Patel shifted uncomfortably in her chair, palms slick against the cushioning of her hands as she handed over a file to her assistant. "Now... everything you need should be here, right down to the hospital's bylaws... I mean, not there – this part is confidential," her voice wavered slightly.

The doctor found herself rubbing her dry lips until they felt almost numb but had difficulty focusing on the task ahead of her despite how tedious it normally would've been. A faint buzzing began in her fingers before dispersing once she stood up to pace around her tiny hospital office space a couple more times, fidgeting with everything not nailed down and talking at an increasingly hushed voice into the still air as if desperate for a distraction.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Lena froze, her eyes fixed on the HR representative as they recited a rehearsed speech about a new employee joining the team. Train my replacement? She must have misheard. A shiver ran down her spine as she imagined herself... redundant. The conference room seemed to shrink, the fluorescent lights humming in a mocking rhythm.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: "What's the plan here?" Emma asked, voice steady but betraying a hint of incredulity. Her boss nodded sympathetically before dropping the bombshell: "We're streamlining teams and, well... you were chosen for your specialized knowledge." A faint tremble began in her fingers as she picked up a pen, her eyes darting between notes on her desk and her boss's expectant expression.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: The phone slipped from Jack's fingers, landing with a thud on the cluttered desktop. "Sorry," he muttered, scrambling to pick it up. The HR rep was already talking about performance metrics and company-wide evaluations – all while asking him to help train the person taking over his role. His hands began to fidget with an intensity he couldn't contain.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: I stared at my supervisor's bland expression, half-expecting a wink or some reassurance that this was all just a silly HR ruse. The words kept repeating in my head: "we're restructuring... you'll be transitioning out..." Like a well-oiled machine, I nodded along, brain fog threatening to overwhelm me as the conversation unfolded around me.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story: Jax's eyes bulged behind horn-rimmed glasses as he mouthed, "You've got to be kidding." The HR rep remained impassive, citing "company growth" and "future-proof strategies." As his head shook on repeat – a slow-motion pendulum of disagreement – the room seemed to tilt, like a seesaw shifting precariously.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Lena stood by the conference room window, gazing out at the gray sky as she listened to her boss's words. "It's time for you to take on more responsibilities, Lena... I need someone with your expertise to train the new team member." His smile was reassuring, but Lena felt a familiar knot form in her stomach.

As she turned back to face him, her eyes met those of her replacement – young, bright-eyed Sarah. Lena forced a nod, trying to hide her unease behind a mask of professionalism. What if this new person didn't learn as quickly? What if they botched projects, tanking the team's reputation?

Walking out to meet Sarah, Lena caught herself fidgeting with her pen, accidentally snapping it in two under the pressure.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Dr. Patel rubbed his tired eyes as he faced the fresh-faced intern standing beside him. "Alright, let's go over the patient charts... and I guess you'll be leading this team from now on." He glanced down at the pile of notes scattered across the counter between them, wondering how someone so young could be entrusted with such a crucial responsibility.

His gaze drifted to the worn armchair in the corner, where he'd spent countless hours listening to patients' stories. The familiar rhythm of his footsteps creaked in protest as he moved towards Sarah. He hesitated for a moment before nodding curtly, trying not to reveal the emptiness growing inside him.

Sarah's enthusiastic questions jolted Dr. Patel back into focus; her determination almost... almost made up for the ache in his chest.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Aila leaned against the kitchen counter, staring blankly at the wall as she recounted the intricacies of the company software to Emma, their replacement intern. When a phone buzzed on the counter nearby, Aila's hand instinctively reached out to silence it, only to realize hers wasn't ringing – it was someone else's.

Their coworker interrupted with a friendly "Hey, how's the transfer going, guys?" The brightness of their tone made Aila want to squint, feeling a sudden fatigue wash over her like a cold draft. She took a step back, eyes drifting around the cramped apartment-turned-office space.

Her hand brushed against Emma's as they passed notes back and forth; in that fleeting moment, something akin to loss flickered across her features before she quickly rearranged them into an encouraging smile.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Sofi scribbled absent-mindedly on a whiteboard as Mark watched over her shoulder. "What do you think of Emma? She's... enthusiastic." The faint whiff of his cologne carried hints of memories Sofi'd thought were long buried – late nights spent sipping coffee with him.

When she finally stepped back, their gazes met for an instant longer than necessary; her eyes dropped to avoid the lingering ache in her chest. "I'm sure Emma's great," Sofi muttered, forcing her gaze away from Mark and onto the blank whiteboard before them.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Emily slid her chair across the empty space of the office, creating a solitary sound that underscored the silence suffocating around her. Their departing manager handed her a file containing Sarah's profile alongside an introduction: "Sarah will primarily work under you for the next few months."

The flickering fluorescent light above hummed as Emily read through the neatly typed pages. Her eyes kept straying back to the image of herself years ago – in happier, more uncertain times. A fragile hope persisted despite reason telling her this chapter would close soon; something a little too familiar stirred within her chest, only gradually subsiding beneath layers of professionalism.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Jamie's eyes rolled in a way that suggested he was tolerating a lecture rather than actually listening. His arms crossed over his chest, making him look like a cranky bear woken from hibernation.

"Okay, so when you're dealing with a particularly tricky client," the manager droned on, "just remember to stay calm and professional." Jamie raised an eyebrow at this advice, as if it was laughable. Hadn't the team discussed this exact scenario just last week?

His thoughts strayed back to his own time in the department. Who had trained him? And how did he end up here, forced to pass on knowledge to a replacement who barely met his standards? Jamie felt his jaw clench, a low growl building in his chest.

"Moving on, you'll need to familiarize yourself with our company software. I've left the tutorial notes on your desk." The manager beamed at him, oblivious to Jamie's darkening mood, like a ray of sunshine breaking through a thunderstorm.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
I slammed my way into the conference room, slamming coffee from my cup as I went. "So, you're 'Sarah'?" I spat out her name like it was a dirty word. My manager looked up from his notes, concerned by my tone.

"Just going over some basics on the company procedure," he said placatingly. I snorted.

"Like what? How to mess around with someone else's work and then pretend you're an expert?" My voice rose in anger, so loud that Sarah shifted uncomfortably in her seat, eyes darting towards my manager for guidance.

My manager's expression turned stern. "Jamie, settle down. This is just a brief orientation." Brief indeed – as long as I'd been working here? They were paying me to babysit this...this replacement of mine?

"Sorry," I muttered, forcing out the word like it was a snake crawling over my tongue.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Dr. Patel leaned against the wall, arms crossed, watching her new trainee fumble with the complex equipment. "Now, first things first: how to use the micro-injector without breaking it." The younger tech's hands danced around the device as he tried to figure it out.

My eyes narrowed as I surveyed this person, their lack of experience already causing trouble in our lab. Who was this newcomer supposed to replace? Me, the resident expert? Unthinkably soon, I'd be leaving and letting some stranger take over. No, I wouldn't say stranger – but definitely amateur. The very thought made my stomach twist with...unease.

I broke away from my observation, clearing my throat abruptly as memories started flooding back: how I used to love the hands-on nature of this job, how it demanded precision and intelligence. Now, handing over that expertise felt like selling out, abandoning ship.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
"Listen carefully," Mr. James said, trying to drill a point through his trainee's vacant expression. He tapped his pen impatiently against his notepad as he went on about supply inventory management. The replacement – some guy I'd never met before – blankly nodded along.

My attention span began to flag like sand trickling from an hourglass, each passing minute bringing us closer to my exit. As inescapable as a shadow that crept up behind you. Where was he going? And wasn't it odd that the company didn't seem to care about keeping veterans like me on hand?

Mr. James's voice droned on; I half-paid attention, my eyes drifting towards the air vent above him. It might as well have been an exhaust pipe – all that went up here stayed here too.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
"Okay, now, how to handle those sticky keyboard problems," our manager chirped, trying for enthusiasm but sounding more like someone announcing a tax hike on breakfast cereal. The young replacement's eyes flickered with interest briefly before his brow creased again in confusion.

As I pretended to listen intently – lips pursed, forehead rumpled – an unshakeable resentment simmered. Something inside me clamped down like my face contorted into a mask of 'friendly instructor'.

The room felt stale and overheated as if the very atmosphere clung to my skin, seeping under fingernails and curling hairs on neck ridges.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Emily's eyes flashed with annoyance as her boss handed her a folder filled with training materials for her replacement. "You're going to train them on their first day," he said, his tone matter-of-fact. Emily felt a surge of heat rise to her face as she forced herself to remain professional. She took the folder and muttered, "Fine." Her voice was tight, barely above a whisper.

As she walked out of the meeting room, Emily's long strides echoed down the hallway. She couldn't help but think that this was ridiculous – who trains someone on their own work? It should be her boss taking care of it, like normal. But no, he wanted her to waste her time spoon-feeding some new hire. She jammed the folder into a drawer and slammed it shut, hard enough that papers ruffled out.

The thought of having to explain everything from scratch made her stomach twist into knots. She felt like crawling out of her own skin, unable to do anything but fume in silence. Her mind wandered to all the things she could be doing instead – real projects, ones that mattered. Not babysitting some newbie.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Jack's face twisted as his manager handed him a bright pink sign with "New Hire Liaison" scribbled on it. "Congratulations!" he said with a forced grin. Jack snatched the sign from his hand and crumpled it into a ball, shoving it into his pocket. What was he really being congratulated for? Being given some dead-end babysitting duty?

He stalked back to his desk, his eyes scanning the cubicles until they landed on Karen, her headset securely in place. Jack stormed over, tapping her shoulder. "You heard?" he growled, trying to keep his voice down but barely succeeding. Karen raised an eyebrow and mouthed something behind him.

Jack watched with growing irritation as Karen chatted with their manager for a few more minutes before glancing back at him. He shook his head and muttered under his breath, stalking off back to his own desk. Now the spotlight was on her – all would be watching how well she handled things.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Maya clenched her jaw as she took in the neatly folded shirt and new hire badge lying on her desk. She'd spent years getting used to being a team leader, figuring out the intricacies of workflow for this one specific department. Just as she was about to get involved with an actual project – one that made her feel like her skills actually mattered! – someone else gets handed her job.

She folded her arms across her chest and leaned back in her chair, surveying the cubicle as if daring anyone to step forward now. Her gaze fell on the new hire's profile picture plastered on a sticky note by her computer monitor – another reminder that this was really happening: she was being replaced.

Her eyes narrowed at the sound of footsteps approaching. Of course it'd be some overeager HR rep with an eager smile and instructions to help the newbie get settled. Maya smiled back on cue, pretending not to know exactly what was going off behind-the-scenes – but all while seething inside.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Heather sat up straight as she listened to her boss explain that she'd be giving daily check-in lessons for the next two weeks. Like clockwork, the thought ticked away in a corner of her mind: this would cut into valuable project time. And didn't he know anything about team morale? What was he thinking, disrupting their rhythm and camaraderie?

Her jaw ticked slightly – she'd caught herself grinding her teeth earlier too often for comfort. Why should someone else get priority over the stuff that needed to be accomplished today? Every new task felt like an itch itching at the corners of her awareness.

When instructed to start training right after lunch, Heather let out a gentle-sounding "Okay" – not to sound eager or accommodating, but because this was all part of corporate protocol now. Her internal monologue simmered and seethed in low heat, while outwardly she agreed without inflection.

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement
story:
Ben's eyes slid away as his manager handed over the materials for training his replacement. "Just show them around, go through key tasks – should take a couple of days," said her measured tone as he listened attentively. It seemed he was now some sort of unofficial mentor, but with no real expertise to claim that responsibility.

The weight on his shoulders started making his collar feel suffocating. If it only took 'a couple of days,' this shouldn't be such a problem – how had things gotten this turned around? Now there were fewer hands and more mouths to feed. All he could do silently seethe within, with every minute spent talking through key procedures a bitter pill in his mind.

As he glanced over at the new recruit hovering by reception – someone who'd have their own chance to wreak havoc one day – Ben muttered under his breath just loud enough for his manager to catch it and roll her eyes.
